CHAPTER VIII
ALTERNATIVES TO THE PROPOSED ACTION
Pursuant to a recent U.S. District Court Order, the Secretary of the Interior is obligated to fully reconsider his earlier approvals of the Tract II and Tract III leases based on this Environmental Impact Statement. His response may be to reapprove the leases as they presently exist, rejection of either or both leases, approval in part or rejection in part, or approval subject to such additional conditions and requirements as he may impose under the applicable laws and regulations. This chapter discusses these alternatives as well as approval subject to new regulations, sources of Tribal income, mining methods, transportation, reclamation, and Tribal entrepreneurship.
The primary purposes of the Crow Tribe's leasing Tract II and Tract III to Westmoreland Resources is to provide certain levels of Tribal income through coal royalties and to make jobs available to Crow Tribal members. National energy needs are a secondary consideration.
LEASE ALTERNATIVES
There are three fundamental alternatives in connection with reconsideration of the leases pursuant to <u>Cady v. Morton</u>. The proposed action is approval of the leases. Alternatively, the leases may be modified or disapproved. The alternatives to the proposed action are discussed below.
Disapproval of the Leases (no action)
Disapproval of the leases equates with "no action" in that there would be no additional development taking place upon Tracts II and III.
